use: Cooking food in boiling water — pasta, eggs, vegetables.

example.ja: パスタ、10分ぐらい茹でて。
example.english: Boil the pasta for about ten minutes.

examplePolite.romaji: pasuta o juppun gurai yudete kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: パスタを10分ぐらい茹でてください。
examplePolite.english: Please boil the pasta for about ten minutes.

notes: Yudetamago = a boiled egg. Just heating water is wakasu.

english: call (over); invite; send for; call (by a name)
use: Not phoning, which is denwa suru.

example.ja: 何て呼べばいい?
example.english: What should I call you?

examplePolite.romaji: nan to yobeba ii desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 何と呼べばいいですか?

notes: Also 'invite': tomodachi o ie ni yobu. Kyuukyuusha yonde! = call an ambulance!

example.ja: ここに名前書いてね。
example.english: Write your name here, okay?

examplePolite.romaji: koko ni onamae o kaite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: ここにお名前を書いてください。

notes: Drawing a picture is also kaku: e o kaku.

english: tell, pass on (a message); get across
use: Passing a message along, or putting feelings into words.

example.ja: 彼によろしく伝えて。
example.english: Say hi to him for me.

examplePolite.ja: 彼によろしく伝えてください。
examplePolite.english: Please say hello to him for me.

notes: Tsutaeru is you telling; tsutawaru is the message getting through.

english: go quiet; shut up; keep (something) quiet

example.ja: なんでずっと黙ってるの?
example.english: Why have you gone so quiet?

examplePolite.romaji: doushite zutto damatte iru n desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: どうしてずっと黙っているんですか?
examplePolite.english: Why have you been so quiet?

notes: Damatte! alone is a blunt 'shut up!'. Oya ni damatte = without telling your parents.

example.ja: この本、もう読んだ?
example.english: Have you read this book yet?

examplePolite.romaji: kono hon wa mou yomimashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: この本はもう読みましたか?
examplePolite.english: Have you read this book yet?

notes: Kuuki o yomu = read the room.

use: Talking about apologising; the words themselves are gomen or sumimasen.

example.romaji: hayaku kanojo ni ayamari na yo.
example.ja: 早く彼女に謝りなよ。
example.english: Go apologise to her, quick.

examplePolite.romaji: hayaku kanojo ni ayamatta hou ga ii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 早く彼女に謝ったほうがいいですよ。
examplePolite.english: You should apologise to her soon.

use: The listener takes ni: tomodachi ni setsumei suru.

example.ja: もう一回説明してくれる?
example.english: Can you explain that again?

examplePolite.romaji: mou ichido setsumei shite itadakemasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: もう一度説明していただけますか?

notes: Also a noun: setsumei ga wakariyasui = the explanation is clear.

use: Introducing people to each other, or pointing someone to a place or service.

example.romaji: dareka ii hito shoukai shite yo.
example.ja: 誰かいい人紹介してよ。
example.english: Introduce me to someone nice.

examplePolite.romaji: dareka ii hito o shoukai shite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 誰かいい人を紹介してください。
examplePolite.english: Please introduce me to someone nice.

use: Declining an invitation, request or offer.

example.ja: 飲み会に誘われたけど、断っちゃった。
example.english: I got invited out drinking but turned it down.

examplePolite.ja: 飲み会に誘われましたが、断りました。
examplePolite.english: I was invited out drinking, but I declined.

notes: On a sign, okotowari shimasu means 'not allowed'.

use: Heard almost only as moushimasu: giving your own name, or staff speaking to customers.

example.ja: はじめまして、田中と申します。
example.english: Nice to meet you, I'm Tanaka.

notes: Never for what others say; for that, use ossharu.

use: Also 'blab': dare ni mo shaberanai de = don't tell anyone.

example.ja: 昨日ずっと友達としゃべってた。
example.english: I was chatting with friends all day yesterday.

examplePolite.romaji: kinou wa zutto tomodachi to shabette imashita.
examplePolite.ja: 昨日はずっと友達としゃべっていました。
examplePolite.english: I was chatting with friends all day yesterday.

notes: More casual than hanasu, and leans toward chatting.

use: Asking someone to come along, or asking someone on a date.

example.romaji: kanojo, eiga ni sasotte miyou ka na.
example.ja: 彼女、映画に誘ってみようかな。
example.english: Maybe I'll ask her to a movie.

examplePolite.romaji: kanojo o eiga ni sasotte miyou to omoimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 彼女を映画に誘ってみようと思います。
examplePolite.english: I think I'll ask her to a movie.

notes: Being invited is sasowareru. Shoutai suru is for formal invitations.

use: Passing on news or results — to a boss, family or friends.

example.ja: 結果出たら報告するね。
example.english: I'll let you know when the results come out.

examplePolite.ja: 結果が出たら報告します。
examplePolite.english: I'll report back when the results come out.

notes: The work motto hourensou = houkoku, renraku, soudan (report, keep in touch, consult).

use: For what a customer, boss or elder says; never for yourself.

example.romaji: shachou ga sou osshatta n da yo.
example.ja: 社長がそうおっしゃったんだよ。
example.english: That's what the boss said.

examplePolite.ja: 社長がそうおっしゃいました。

notes: The polite form is irregular: osshaimasu. Ossharu toori desu = you're quite right.

example.ja: 今日、部長に褒められた!
example.english: My manager praised me today!

examplePolite.ja: 今日、部長に褒められました。

notes: Often heard in the passive: homerareta = I got praised.

english: get across; come through; be passed down
use: When a message or feeling reaches the other person: tsutawatta? = did that make sense?

example.romaji: kimochi, chanto tsutawatta to omou yo.
example.ja: 気持ち、ちゃんと伝わったと思うよ。
example.english: I think your feelings really came across.

examplePolite.romaji: kimochi wa chanto tsutawatta to omoimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 気持ちはちゃんと伝わったと思います。
examplePolite.english: I think your feelings came across.

notes: The person tsutaeru; the message tsutawaru.

english: greet; say hello; give a short speech
use: Saying hello properly, or a formal few words at an event.

example.romaji: tonari no hito ni aisatsu shita?
example.ja: 隣の人に挨拶した?
example.english: Did you say hello to the neighbours?

examplePolite.romaji: tonari no kata ni aisatsu shimashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: 隣の方に挨拶しましたか?
examplePolite.english: Did you say hello to the neighbours?

notes: Aisatsu ni iku = pay a courtesy visit (new neighbours, in-laws).

english: boast, show off; be proud of

example.ja: また彼女の自慢してる。
example.english: He's bragging about his girlfriend again.

examplePolite.romaji: mata kanojo no jiman o shite imasu.
examplePolite.ja: また彼女の自慢をしています。
examplePolite.english: He's bragging about his girlfriend again.

notes: Jiman no musuko = a son someone is proud of. Jiman ja nai kedo = not to brag, but.

use: Mostly in set business phrases: onegai moushiagemasu, owabi moushiagemasu.

example.ja: 今後ともよろしくお願い申し上げます。
example.english: We look forward to working with you going forward.

notes: Heard in speeches, announcements and business email; mousu is the lighter version.
